chunks: 2608 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
“If the muhrim is compelled to wear a cloak made of bard and cannot find any garment other than it, then he should wear it inside out and not insert his hands into the sleeves of the cloak.”

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in the state of ihram
key_terms.بَرْدٍ: striped cloth or a type of woven garment material
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.يَدَيِ الْقَبَاءِ: the two sleeves/openings of the cloak

ai.seo_question: What should a muhrim do if he is forced to wear a qaba’ and has no other garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in the state of ihram who is compelled by necessity to wear a qaba’. If no other garment is available, he may wear it in an altered manner—inside out and without placing his hands into its sleeves—thus limiting the normal form of prohibited dress in ihram.
